findings.claim: The token expiry deadline is not enforced while a delivery is being authorized or enqueued, so a protected mutation can be emitted after the verified token has expired.
findings.evidence: In `run_producer`, `sleep_until(producer.deadline)` is only one branch of the `tokio::select!` that waits for the next raw item; after an item is received the code awaits `delivery_frame(&producer, delivery).await` and then `tx.try_send(frame)` without rechecking `producer.deadline` (lines 87-141). The acceptance criteria require authority lifetime/revocation boundaries to meet the watch contract and per-event authority enforcement.
findings.suggested_fix: Race the entire per-delivery authorization/build/enqueue path against `producer.deadline`, or explicitly check `Instant::now() >= producer.deadline` immediately before issuing checkpoints and before `try_send`; apply the same deadline check in initial snapshot enqueue.
